description.p: Mirza turns your voice into text in any program. Press a shortcut, speak, and your words are typed wherever your cursor is: your editor, browser, chat apps, email or terminal.
It uses a cloud speech-to-text service of your choice (Soniox, OpenAI or ElevenLabs) with your own API key, and it handles several languages in the same sentence, such as Persian and English.

ul.li: Global shortcuts: press to start and stop, or hold to talk
Real-time transcription, typed as you speak each phrase
Works on Wayland and X11, including KDE Plasma and GNOME
Tray icon, usage and spend overview, proxy support

description.p: Voice tasks get a "Your own rules" box, on the desktop and on Android: rules for the AI that reads your tasks, such as "Write the title in English.", which win over Mirza's own. The voice tasks guide also explains the "invalid_request" error at Google sign-in.

Soniox now uses its v6 model and gets the API key in a header. Update before 15 January 2027: from then on Soniox refuses the key the way 0.1.5 sends it. New and optional: AI revision, a separate shortcut that lets Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter or your own server drop fillers and repeats, keep your last correction and fix punctuation and half-spaces; if the AI fails, the text is typed as you said it. Also new: voice tasks, a task shortcut that saves what you say as a short task in the right Google Tasks list, plus a Google Calendar event when you said a time, with Undo and Edit in the notification. Mirza is now also an app for Android phones.

On Windows, notifications show Mirza's name and icon instead of Windows PowerShell's. On Windows and macOS, Mirza uses the system proxy that VPN apps set. Network errors are explained in plain words with a hint about the proxy, and a Soniox connection that stops answering is reported after 10 seconds instead of hanging. On Linux, the start and stop sounds no longer go silent when notification sounds are muted.

A short sound when dictation starts and stops, and a notice when a new version is out. On KDE Plasma 6.3, System Settings no longer opens every time Mirza starts. The usage page shows when it is refreshing and whether it worked, and recent text can be cleared.

Fixes text not being typed on KDE Plasma ("you left the window you started in") when KWin reports an empty activation right after the real one. Each shortcut press now arrives once, even after the shortcuts are changed.
Default shortcuts: Ctrl+Alt+H to start and stop, Ctrl+Alt+J to hold and talk. The shortcut recorder handles the Meta key, and Mirza keeps one consistent name in the desktop's shortcut settings.
App icons in every size and a proper app description for software centers.
